title: Infection, hygiene and safety words
blurb: Define the words for germs, spread, outbreaks, harm and protection, and keep sterile, aseptic and septic apart.
question: “The exposed nurses were placed in quarantine, and the infected patient was isolated in a room cleaned with aseptic technique.” Why are quarantine and isolation different words, and is aseptic the same as sterile?

teach.h: Words for germs, spread and protection
teach.body: Infection and safety words describe disease-causing germs, how they spread, how outbreaks are sized and how people are protected. Formally, they are the terms of infection control and environmental safety. Plain English: they say what is dirty, what is clean, what spreads, and what keeps people safe. The HESI A2 tests the meaning of the word only; it never asks you to know a hospital procedure.

bands.label: Disinfected: germs killed on a surface

teach.caption: Asepsis (n) is the germ-free state; contaminate (v) and disinfect (v) are actions that move an object down or up the scale.

head: Word
Meaning
Near miss
teach.caption: Contagious and communicable overlap; the HESI will not ask you to choose between them.
Endemic = regular and local. Epidemic = sudden and widespread. Pandemic = worldwide.

teach.h: Scenario: Sofia reads a health department notice
teach.body: Sofia, a practical nursing applicant, reads a county notice: “Measles is not endemic here, but an epidemic in a nearby county has reached 40 cases. The virus is highly contagious, and its incubation period is about 10 to 12 days. Unvaccinated people who were exposed will be placed in quarantine. Anyone not yet inoculated should take this precaution now.”

items: Not endemic: measles is not regularly present in her county.
Epidemic: a sudden, widespread outbreak in one region, not worldwide (that would be a pandemic).
Contagious: spread by contact. Incubation: the time from exposure to first symptoms.
Quarantine: exposed people who are not yet sick are separated to see whether they become ill.
Inoculated, precaution: vaccinated; a step taken in advance to prevent harm.

teach.text: Sterile means free of ALL microorganisms; aseptic means free of disease-causing ones; septic means infected; an antiseptic is the germ-killing agent. And watch the sound-alikes: noxious (harmful) is not nauseous (causing nausea), and deleterious (damaging) is not delirious (confused).

items: Septic infected; aseptic free of pathogens; sterile free of all microorganisms; antiseptic kills germs.
Pathogen causes disease; vector carries it; a carrier spreads it without being ill.
Endemic regular and local; epidemic sudden and regional; pandemic worldwide.
Isolate the sick; quarantine the exposed. Incubation = exposure to first symptoms.
Noxious and deleterious mean harmful; immune means protected; inoculate means vaccinate.

summary: You can now define the words for germs, spread, outbreak size, harm and protection. You can also separate the look-alikes the HESI A2 uses as traps: septic, aseptic and sterile; endemic, epidemic and pandemic; isolation and quarantine; noxious and nauseous.

A.q: Dropping the gauze on the floor would contaminate it, so the nurse opened a fresh package. What is the best definition of the word “contaminate” in this sentence?
A.why: Contaminate means to make impure or unclean, especially by introducing germs.

whyNot.0: A dry floor would not soak the gauze; contaminate is about germs, not moisture.
whyNot.2: Tearing damages the gauze; contaminating makes it unclean.
whyNot.3: Making germ-free is decontaminate or sterilize, the opposite.

A.q: Good hand hygiene remains one of the simplest ways to reduce infections in a busy clinic. What is the best definition of the word “hygiene” in this sentence?
A.why: Hygiene is the set of practices that keep people and their surroundings clean and healthy.

whyNot.1: Protective clothing, such as gloves, is equipment, not hygiene itself.
whyNot.2: Testing for germs identifies them; hygiene keeps them away.
whyNot.3: Moisturizing cares for the skin but is not what hygiene means.

A.q: Officials sprayed the marshes because mosquitoes are the main vector for West Nile virus in the county. What is the best definition of the word “vector” in this sentence?
A.why: A vector is an organism, such as a mosquito or tick, that carries a disease to another host.

whyNot.0: The cause of the disease is the pathogen (the virus); the mosquito only carries it.
whyNot.1: A symptom is something the patient feels, not an organism.
whyNot.3: A disease-free zone is a place, not an organism.

B.q: Although none of the crew felt sick, they remained in quarantine until their test results came back. What is the best definition of the word “quarantine” in this sentence?
B.why: Quarantine separates people who were exposed to a disease but are not sick, to see whether they become ill.

whyNot.0: Separating people who are already ill is isolation; the crew felt well.
whyNot.1: Vaccination prevents disease; quarantine is separation.
whyNot.2: The crew are not patients; quarantine is not a hospital stay.

B.q: Lyme disease is endemic in parts of the northeastern United States and the upper Midwest. What is the best definition of the word “endemic” in this sentence?
B.why: Endemic means regularly present in a particular area or population.

whyNot.1: A sudden spread is an epidemic.
whyNot.3: Wiped out is eradicated, the opposite of regularly present.

B.q: The label warns that the drain cleaner releases noxious vapors if it is mixed with bleach. What is the best definition of the word “noxious” in this sentence?

whyNot.0: Causing nausea is nauseous, the classic sound-alike.
whyNot.1: Visibility is unrelated; many noxious vapors cannot be seen.
whyNot.3: Rude and offensive is obnoxious, usually said of people.

C.q: Researchers studied the deleterious effects of poor sleep on memory in first-year nursing students. What is the best definition of the word “deleterious” in this sentence?

whyNot.0: Delayed is a meaning that fits the topic loosely, but deleterious means harmful.

C.q: Which word names a person who harbors a pathogen and can spread it without being ill?
C.why: A carrier harbors and can spread a pathogen without being ill.

whyNot.0: A vector is usually an insect or animal, such as a mosquito or tick, that transmits disease.
whyNot.1: A patient is someone receiving care, usually because they are ill.
whyNot.2: The pathogen is the germ itself, not the person who harbors it.

C.q: Doctors feared the virulent strain because it caused pneumonia even in young, healthy adults. What is the best definition of the word “virulent” in this sentence?
C.why: In a medical sentence, virulent means highly harmful and able to cause severe disease.

whyNot.0: Caused by a virus is viral, a look-alike.
whyNot.2: Speed of spread is not virulence; virulence is how severe the disease is.
whyNot.3: A new strain may be virulent or mild; virulent describes harm.

reteach.title: A kitchen and a rumor
reteach.question: Think about a kitchen counter and a rumor at school. Could everyday cleaning and gossip help you hold onto infection words?

blocks.body: Raw chicken juice on a counter contaminates it. Spraying it with bleach disinfects it. A brand-new, sealed surgical glove is sterile: nothing living on it at all. Now the rumor: the person who starts it is like the pathogen, the friend who passes it along without believing it is the carrier, and a rumor that stays in one homeroom all year is endemic. When it sweeps the whole school in a day, it is an epidemic; when it reaches every school in the country, a pandemic.

blocks.text: The analogy helps with scale only. Keep the exact meanings: endemic regular and local, epidemic sudden and widespread, pandemic across countries.

explain.body: Septic means infected. Contaminate means to make impure. Disinfect means to kill germs on a surface. Aseptic means free of pathogens. Sterile means free of all microorganisms.

test.q: The nurse used aseptic technique to change the dressing on Mr. Cho's surgical wound. What is the best definition of the word “aseptic” in this sentence?
test.why: Aseptic means free of disease-causing microorganisms.

whyNot.0: Infected is septic; the a- prefix means without.
whyNot.2: Germ-killing describes an antiseptic agent, not a germ-free state.
whyNot.3: Timing fits a procedure loosely, but aseptic is about germs.

explain.body: Endemic means regularly present in one area. An epidemic is a sudden, widespread outbreak in a community or region. A pandemic spreads across countries or the world.

test.q: The pandemic disrupted air travel on every continent for nearly two years. What is the best definition of the word “pandemic” in this sentence?
test.why: A pandemic is an outbreak that spreads across countries or the world.

whyNot.1: An outbreak in one community or region is an epidemic.
whyNot.2: A disease regularly present in one area is endemic.
whyNot.3: A wild uproar is pandemonium, a look-alike.

explain.body: A pathogen causes disease; a vector carries it between hosts; a carrier spreads it without being ill. Contagious means spread by contact; virulent means causing severe disease. Incubation is the time from exposure to the first symptoms.

test.q: Because the incubation period can last two weeks, exposed staff were checked daily for 14 days. What is the best definition of the word “incubation” in this sentence?
options: time a vaccine takes to work
test.why: Incubation is the time between exposure to an infection and the first symptoms.

whyNot.0: Recovery comes after the illness; that is convalescence.
whyNot.1: The length of the illness starts with symptoms; incubation ends there.
whyNot.2: Vaccine response time is not incubation.

explain.body: Toxic means poisonous; noxious and deleterious mean harmful; hazardous means dangerous. Immune means protected; inoculate means to give a vaccine; a precaution is a step taken in advance to prevent harm.

test.q: Nurses at the travel clinic inoculate travelers against yellow fever before certain trips abroad. What is the best definition of the word “inoculate” in this sentence?
test.why: Inoculate means to introduce a vaccine into the body to produce immunity.

whyNot.0: Examining is assessing; it gives no protection.
whyNot.2: Instructing echoes inculcate, a look-alike meaning to teach by repetition.
whyNot.3: Isolating separates a person; it does not vaccinate.
